extracted.intended_audience: general public and potential nominators/interested researchers about the MacArthur Fellows Program
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the MacArthur Fellows Program's eligibility, selection qualities, nomination and review procedures, award amount and distribution, and program purpose — i.e., the criteria and processes used to identify and name MacArthur Fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. citizens or residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are "citizens or residents of the United States."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is limited to individuals who are U.S. citizens or residents; no other nationality/ residency categories are specified on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of work — any field
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is awarded to individuals "working in any field."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation groups recipients into five broad categories (Arts, Humanities, Public Issues, STEM, and Social Sciences) but explicitly awards fellows across any field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core selection qualities — originality, dedication, self-direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to individuals who have shown "extraordinary originality and dedication in their creative pursuits and a marked capacity for self-direction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quoted phrase serves as the principal evaluative standard for identifying fellows; emphasis is on originality, sustained commitment (dedication), and ability to direct one's own work (self-direction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship purpose — investment in originality, insight, and potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation states: "the fellowship is not a reward for past accomplishments but rather an investment in a person's originality, insight, and potential" (while also noting such potential is "based on a track record of significant accomplishments").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection aims to identify current originality and future potential rather than merely rewarding past achievements; however, evidence of a track record of significant accomplishments is used to assess potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application pathway — nomination-only (no applications accepted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program "does not accept applications." Instead, "anonymous and confidential nominations are invited by the foundation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals cannot apply directly; candidacy depends on being nominated by others invited by the foundation. This procedural rule strongly shapes how potential fellows are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations and the selection process are described as "anonymous and confidential."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both nominations and the committee-level review are kept anonymous/confidential — this affects transparency and who can know or publicize candidacy before selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee review and recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: An "anonymous and confidential selection committee of about a dozen people" reviews all nominees and "recommends recipients to the president and board of directors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final appointment is via committee review followed by recommendation to the foundation's leadership; committee membership, deliberations, and nominations are kept confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of fellows awarded annually
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation typically awards the prize "to typically between 20 and 30 individuals" each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program scale: selection is limited to a relatively small cohort annually, which constrains competitive intensity and implies selective standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and payment terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the prize is "$800,000 paid over five years in quarterly installments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is a multi-year, lump-sum-like stipend disbursed quarterly over five years. The page also notes historical amounts (previously $625,000, earlier $500,000) and that the award is regarded as "no strings attached."

rubrics_metrics.name: No-strings-attached character
rubrics_metrics.description: The award has been called "one of the most significant awards that is truly 'no strings attached'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients receive the funds without explicit programmatic restrictions governing how the money must be used; this is part of the program's stated intent to support creative freedom and potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "Most new fellows learn of their nomination and award upon receiving a congratulatory phone call."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is typically personal and immediate (phone call); this is a procedural feature rather than an evaluative selection criterion but is part of the program's operating norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology guidance — avoid 'genius' label
rubrics_metrics.description: The MacArthur Foundation "does not use the term 'genius' to describe its fellows and has asked the media to stop using it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications about the program and its recipients should avoid the colloquial 'genius' label; this reflects the foundation's preferred framing of the fellowship.
